results.title: Kourovka Problem 11.42 (statement)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that there is a torsion-free group $G$ (no element of $G$ other than the identity has finite order) that has exactly three conjugacy classes and has a subgroup of index $2$.

results.title: Minasyan's theorem (Kourovka Problem 11.42)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a torsion-free group $G$ (no element of $G$ other than the identity has finite order) that has exactly three conjugacy classes and has a subgroup of index $2$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 11.67 (statement)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that there is a torsion-free group $G$ (no element of $G$ other than the identity has finite order) with exactly three conjugacy classes in which no element $g \neq 1$ is conjugate to its inverse $g^{-1}$, that is, no nontrivial conjugacy class contains a pair of mutually inverse elements.

results.title: Bagayoko's theorem (Kourovka Problem 11.67)

results.title: Units of the Gaussian integers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A Gaussian integer $x \in \mathbb{Z}[i]$ is a unit if and only if $x$ is one of $1$, $-1$, $i$ and $-i$.

results.title: Gaussian integers of prime norm are prime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\pi = a + bi \in \mathbb{Z}[i]$ and let $N(\pi) = a^2 + b^2$ be its norm. If the absolute value of $N(\pi)$ is a prime number, then $\pi$ is a prime element of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$.

results.title: 1 + i is a Gaussian prime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Gaussian integer $1 + i$ is a prime element of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$; its norm is $2$.

results.title: Factorization of 2 in the Gaussian integers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ we have $2 = -i \cdot (1 + i)^2$, where $-i$ is a unit with inverse $i$.

results.title: Enumeration of the Gaussian units
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The map $u$ on $\{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ with $u_0 = 1$, $u_1 = -1$, $u_2 = i$ and $u_3 = -i$ in $\mathbb{Z}[i]$, listing the four units of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$.

results.title: The four Gaussian units are distinct
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $u_0 = 1$, $u_1 = -1$, $u_2 = i$ and $u_3 = -i$ in $\mathbb{Z}[i]$. For $j, k \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$, if $u_j = u_k$ then $j = k$.

results.title: The enumeration of the Gaussian units is complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $u_0 = 1$, $u_1 = -1$, $u_2 = i$ and $u_3 = -i$. Every unit $u$ of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ equals $u_j$ for some $j \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$.

results.title: Inverses of the Gaussian units
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The map $v$ on $\{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ with $v_0 = 1$, $v_1 = -1$, $v_2 = -i$ and $v_3 = i$ in $\mathbb{Z}[i]$, listing the inverses of the units $1$, $-1$, $i$ and $-i$ in that order.

results.title: Each Gaussian unit times its listed inverse is one
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Explicit Gaussian prime factors of a prime congruent to 1 mod 4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$. Then there are natural numbers $a$ and $b$ with $a^2 + b^2 = p$ such that both $a + bi$ and $a - bi$ are prime elements of the Gaussian integers $\mathbb{Z}[i]$.

results.title: Classification of the Gaussian primes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every prime element $z$ of the Gaussian integers $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ is associated to one of the following: a rational prime $p$ with $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$; one of $a + bi$ and $a - bi$, where $a$ and $b$ are natural numbers with $a^2 + b^2 = p$ for some rational prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$; or $1 + i$.

results.title: Primes congruent to 1 mod 4 split in the Gaussian integers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$. Then there is a prime element $\pi = a + bi$ of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ whose norm $N(\pi) = a^2 + b^2$ equals $p$.

results.title: Factoring a prime as a Gaussian integer times its conjugate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, write $N(a + bi) = a^2 + b^2$ for the norm on $\mathbb{Z}[i]$, and let $\pi \in \mathbb{Z}[i]$ satisfy $N(\pi) = p$. Then $p = \pi \bar{\pi}$ in $\mathbb{Z}[i]$, where $\bar{\pi}$ is the complex conjugate of $\pi$, and $\bar{\pi}$ is a prime element of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$.

results.title: Gaussian integers of split prime norm are not associate to their conjugates
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $N(a + bi) = a^2 + b^2$ for the norm on $\mathbb{Z}[i]$. Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ and let $\pi \in \mathbb{Z}[i]$ satisfy $N(\pi) = p$. Then the complex conjugate $\bar{\pi}$ is not associated to $\pi$: there is no unit $u$ of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ with $\bar{\pi} u = \pi$.

results.title: Number of Gaussian integers of norm a power of a split prime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $N(a + bi) = a^2 + b^2$ for the norm on $\mathbb{Z}[i]$. Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, let $e$ be a natural number, and suppose $\pi \in \mathbb{Z}[i]$ is a prime element with $N(\pi) = p$. Then exactly $4(e + 1)$ Gaussian integers $\alpha$ satisfy $|N(\alpha)| = p^e$.

results.title: Invertible fractional ideals have nonzero absolute norm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain that is a free $\mathbb{Z}$-module of finite rank, and let $F$ be its field of fractions. For every invertible fractional ideal $I$ of $R$ in $F$, the absolute norm of $I$, a rational number, is nonzero.

results.title: Invertible fractional ideals have positive absolute norm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain that is a free $\mathbb{Z}$-module of finite rank, and let $F$ be its field of fractions. For every invertible fractional ideal $I$ of $R$ in $F$, the absolute norm of $I$, a rational number, is positive.

results.title: Arakelov divisor
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. An Arakelov divisor on $K$ is a pair $(I, r)$, where $I$ is an invertible fractional ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ in $K$ and $r$ assigns a positive real number $r_w$ to each infinite place $w$ of $K$.

results.title: Archimedean factor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $D = (I, r)$ be an Arakelov divisor on a number field $K$. Its archimedean factor is the positive real number $\prod_w r_w^{m_w}$, where the product runs over all infinite places $w$ of $K$ and $m_w$ is $1$ if $w$ is real and $2$ if $w$ is complex.

results.title: Archimedean factor as a real number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D = (I, r)$ be an Arakelov divisor on a number field $K$, and for each infinite place $w$ of $K$ let $m_w$ be $1$ if $w$ is real and $2$ if $w$ is complex. Viewed as a real number, the archimedean factor of $D$ equals the real product $\prod_w r_w^{m_w}$ over all infinite places $w$ of $K$.

results.title: Ideal norm of an Arakelov divisor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an Arakelov divisor $D$ of a number field $K$ with invertible fractional ideal $I$, the ideal norm of $D$ is the absolute norm $N(I)$ of $I$, regarded as a positive real number; it is positive because $I$ is invertible.

results.title: Real value of the ideal norm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every Arakelov divisor $D$ of a number field $K$ with fractional ideal $I$, the ideal norm of $D$, viewed as a real number, equals the absolute norm $N(I) \in \mathbb{Q}$ of $I$, viewed as a real number.

results.title: Archimedean factor homomorphism
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a number field $K$, the map sending an Arakelov divisor on $K$ to its archimedean factor is a monoid homomorphism from the Arakelov divisors on $K$, multiplied componentwise, to the positive real numbers under multiplication.

results.title: Ideal norm homomorphism
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a number field $K$, the map sending an Arakelov divisor $(I, r)$ on $K$ to the absolute norm of $I$, viewed as a positive real number, is a monoid homomorphism from the Arakelov divisors on $K$, multiplied componentwise, to the positive real numbers under multiplication.

results.title: Size of an Arakelov divisor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a number field $K$, the size homomorphism sends an Arakelov divisor $D = (I, (r_w)_w)$, with $I$ an invertible fractional ideal of the ring of integers of $K$ and $r_w > 0$ for each infinite place $w$, to the positive real number $\prod_w r_w^{m_w} / N(I)$, where $w$ runs over the infinite places of $K$, $m_w$ is $1$ for a real place and $2$ for a complex place, and $N(I)$ is the absolute norm of $I$. It is a…

results.title: Size as a quotient of homomorphisms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every Arakelov divisor $D$ of a number field $K$, the size of $D$ equals the archimedean-factor homomorphism evaluated at $D$ divided by the ideal-norm homomorphism evaluated at $D$, the quotient taken in the group of positive reals.

results.title: Explicit formula for the size of an Arakelov divisor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D = (I, (r_w)_w)$ be an Arakelov divisor of a number field $K$, where $I$ is an invertible fractional ideal of the ring of integers of $K$ and $r_w > 0$ for each infinite place $w$ of $K$. For each $w$ let $m_w$ be $1$ if $w$ is real and $2$ if $w$ is complex, and let $N(I)$ be the absolute norm of $I$. Then the size of $D$, as a real number, is

results.title: Section set of an Arakelov divisor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $D$ be an Arakelov divisor of a number field $K$, with invertible fractional ideal $I$ and positive real number $r_w$ at each infinite place $w$ of $K$. The section set of $D$ is the set of $x \in I$ such that $w(x) \le r_w$ for every infinite place $w$ of $K$.

results.title: Membership in the section set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D$ be an Arakelov divisor of a number field $K$, with invertible fractional ideal $I$ and positive real number $r_w$ at each infinite place $w$ of $K$. An element $x \in K$ lies in the section set of $D$ if and only if $x \in I$ and $w(x) \le r_w$ for every infinite place $w$ of $K$.

results.title: Finiteness of section sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every Arakelov divisor $D$ of a number field $K$, the section set of $D$ is finite.

results.title: Archimedean part of a principal divisor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a nonzero element $x$ of a number field $K$, this is the family that assigns to each infinite place $w$ of $K$ the positive real number $w(x)$.

results.title: Principal Arakelov divisor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a nonzero element $x$ of a number field $K$, the principal Arakelov divisor of $x$ consists of the principal fractional ideal $x\mathcal{O}_K$ together with the positive real number $w(x)$ at each infinite place $w$ of $K$.

results.title: Infinite component of a principal divisor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field, $x \in K$ nonzero and $w$ an infinite place of $K$. The positive real number that the principal Arakelov divisor of $x$ assigns to $w$ is $w(x)$, the absolute value of $x$ at $w$.

results.title: Finite component of a principal divisor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. For every nonzero $x \in K$, the fractional ideal component of the principal Arakelov divisor of $x$ is the principal fractional ideal $x\mathcal{O}_K$.

results.title: Principal divisor homomorphism
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a number field $K$, the map sending a nonzero element $x \in K$ to its principal Arakelov divisor is a group homomorphism from the multiplicative group $K^\times$ to the group of Arakelov divisors of $K$.

results.title: Subgroup of principal Arakelov divisors
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a number field $K$, the principal subgroup is the image of the principal divisor homomorphism, that is, the subgroup of the group of Arakelov divisors of $K$ consisting of the principal Arakelov divisors of the nonzero elements of $K$.

results.title: Degree-zero Arakelov divisors
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a number field $K$, the degree-zero subgroup of the group of Arakelov divisors on $K$ is the kernel of the size homomorphism, that is, the subgroup of Arakelov divisors of size $1$.

results.title: Principal Arakelov divisors have size one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. For every nonzero $x \in K$, the principal Arakelov divisor of $x$, formed by the principal fractional ideal $x\mathcal{O}_K$ and the values $w(x)$ at the infinite places $w$ of $K$, has size $1$.

results.title: Principal Arakelov divisors have degree zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a number field $K$, the subgroup of principal Arakelov divisors of $K$ is contained in the degree-zero subgroup.

results.title: Large Arakelov divisors have a nonzero section
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field with $s$ complex places and discriminant $d_K$, and let $D$ be an Arakelov divisor on $K$. If the size of $D$ is strictly greater than $(2/\pi)^s \sqrt{|d_K|}$, then the section set of $D$ contains a nonzero element of $K$.

results.title: Bounded representation by $x^2 + y^2 - z^2$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $n$ has a bounded representation by $x^2 + y^2 - z^2$ if there are natural numbers $x, y, z$ with $n = x^2 + y^2 - z^2$ and $x^2 \le n$, $y^2 \le n$, $z^2 \le n$, where the subtraction is truncated subtraction of natural numbers.

results.title: Representation by $x^2 + y^2 - z^2$ with the bound $n + 2\sqrt{n}$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $n$ has this representation if there are natural numbers $x, y, z$ with $n = x^2 + y^2 - z^2$, where the subtraction is truncated subtraction of natural numbers, and each of $x^2$, $y^2$, $z^2$ is at most $n + 2\sqrt{n}$ as a real number.

results.title: Strict width monotonicity of Lorentzian integrals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let `μ` be a finite measure on `ℝ` (the zero measure included) and `0 < Γ₁ < Γ₂`. Then `∫ E, Γ₁ ^ 2 / (E ^ 2 + Γ₁ ^ 2) ∂μ < ∫ E, Γ₂ ^ 2 / (E ^ 2 + Γ₂ ^ 2) ∂μ` if and only if `μ` gives positive mass to `{0}ᶜ`. The kernel equals `1` at `E = 0` for every width, so mass at the origin never contributes to the increase; in particular the zero measure, and any multiple of the Dirac mass at `0`, give equal integrals.

results.title: Lorentzian integrals are nondecreasing in the width
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let `μ` be a finite measure on `ℝ`; it is nonnegative by type and may be the zero measure. If `0 < Γ₁ ≤ Γ₂`, then `∫ E, Γ₁ ^ 2 / (E ^ 2 + Γ₁ ^ 2) ∂μ ≤ ∫ E, Γ₂ ^ 2 / (E ^ 2 + Γ₂ ^ 2) ∂μ`. Both widths are integrated against the same measure, and equal widths are allowed.

results.title: Partitions with unique subsums except one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The partitions of $m$ contained in a partition $\lambda$ are the distinct sub-multisets of the parts of $\lambda$ with sum $m$. Let $v \ge 1$. There are a natural number $n$ and a partition $\lambda$ of $n$ that contains exactly $v$ partitions of some $m$ with $v \le m \le n - v$ and exactly one partition of every positive integer $m' < n$ other than $m$ if and only if $v = 1$ or $v = 2$.

results.title: Number of subpartitions with a given sum
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a multiset $\lambda$ of natural numbers and $m \in \mathbb{N}$, the number of partitions of $m$ contained in $\lambda$ is the number of distinct sub-multisets of $\lambda$ whose elements sum to $m$.

results.title: Perfect partition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. A multiset $\lambda$ of natural numbers is a perfect partition of $n$ when its elements are positive, they sum to $n$, and for every integer $m$ with $1 \le m \le n$ exactly one partition of $m$ is contained in $\lambda$, that is, exactly one sub-multiset of $\lambda$ has sum $m$ (equal sub-multisets are counted once).

results.title: Double-perfect partitions of higher order
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A double-perfect partition of $N$ of order $r$ is a finite multiset $\lambda$ of positive integers with sum $N$ such that, for every integer $m$ with $1 \le m \le N$, the number of distinct sub-multisets of $\lambda$ with sum $m$ is $2$ if $r + 1 \le m \le N - r - 1$ and $1$ otherwise. Their set is denoted $U_r(N)$; order $1$ gives the double-perfect partitions.

results.title: Type-A double-perfect partition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $r$ and $N$ be natural numbers. A multiset $\lambda$ of natural numbers is a Type-A double-perfect partition of $N$ of order $r$ when $\lambda$ is a double-perfect partition of $N$ of order $r$ and there is a perfect partition $\beta$ of $N - r - 1$ (read as $0$ when $N \le r$) such that $\lambda$ is $\beta$ with $r + 1$ parts equal to $1$ added, or $\beta$ with one part equal to $r + 1$ added. The set of these…

results.title: MacMahon's partition of an ordered factorization
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: To a finite sequence $(a_1, \dots, a_k)$ of natural numbers, read as the ordered factorization $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_k$, attach the multiset of parts $(1^{a_1-1}, a_1^{a_2-1}, (a_1a_2)^{a_3-1}, \dots, (a_1\cdots a_{k-1})^{a_k-1})$, where $x^e$ denotes $e$ parts equal to $x$ and an exponent $a_i - 1$ is read as $0$ when $a_i = 0$. In particular the empty sequence gives the empty multiset.

results.title: MacMahon's partition of the factorization 2 · 3
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: MacMahon's bijection sends the ordered factorization $6 = 2 \cdot 3$ to the partition $(1, 2^2) = (1, 2, 2)$ of $5$.

results.title: The partition of a factorization sums to the product minus one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k \ge 0$ and let $a_1, \dots, a_k \ge 1$ be integers. The parts of the partition $(1^{a_1-1}, a_1^{a_2-1}, (a_1a_2)^{a_3-1}, \dots, (a_1\cdots a_{k-1})^{a_k-1})$ that MacMahon's bijection attaches to the ordered factorization $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_k$, where $x^e$ denotes $e$ parts equal to $x$, sum to $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_k - 1$.

results.title: Truncated recursion for ordered factorizations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, define $f_k(n)$ by recursion on $k$: $f_0(n) = 0$, $f_{k+1}(1) = 1$, and for $n \ne 1$, $f_{k+1}(n)$ is the sum of $f_k(d)$ over the proper divisors $d$ of $n$, that is, the divisors $d$ of $n$ with $1 \le d < n$ (there are none when $n = 0$).

results.title: Number of ordered factorizations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \ge 2$, $f(n)$ is the number of ordered factorizations $n = a_1 a_2 \cdots a_k$ of $n$ into factors $a_i > 1$ (OEIS A074206); moreover $f(0) = 0$ and $f(1) = 1$.

results.title: The truncated ordered-factorization recursion stabilizes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f_k(n)$ be the truncated recursion with $f_0(n) = 0$, $f_{k+1}(1) = 1$, and $f_{k+1}(n)$ the sum of $f_k(d)$ over the proper divisors $d$ of $n$ when $n \ne 1$. For all natural numbers $n$ and $k$ with $n \le k$, $f_k(n) = f(n)$, where $f(n)$ is the number of ordered factorizations of $n$ into factors greater than $1$.

results.title: Recursion for the number of ordered factorizations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every integer $n \ge 2$, the number $f(n)$ of ordered factorizations of $n$ into factors greater than $1$ satisfies $f(n) = \sum_{d \mid n,\ d < n} f(d)$, the sum running over the proper divisors $d$ of $n$.

results.title: Small values of the ordered factorization count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The number $f(n)$ of ordered factorizations of $n$ into factors greater than $1$ takes the values $f(0) = 0$, $f(1) = 1$, $f(6) = 3$ and $f(12) = 8$.

results.title: A perfect partition of seven
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The partition $(1^3, 4)$ of $7$, with three parts equal to $1$ and one part equal to $4$, is a perfect partition of $7$.

results.title: A Type-A double-perfect partition of seven
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The partition $(1^5, 2)$ of $7$, with five parts equal to $1$ and one part equal to $2$, is a Type-A double-perfect partition of $7$ of order $1$.

results.title: Lee's count of double-perfect partitions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f(m)$ be the number of ordered factorizations of $m$ into factors greater than $1$, with $f(0) = 0$ and $f(1) = 1$. For every $n \ge 4$, the number $d(n)$ of double-perfect partitions of $n$ of order $1$ is $f(n-1)$ unless $n \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, in which case $d(n) = f(n-1) - f((n-1)/4)$.

results.title: Double-perfect partitions from perfect partitions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N > 3$. A multiset $\lambda$ of natural numbers is a double-perfect partition of $N$ of order $1$ if and only if there is a perfect partition $\beta$ of $N - 2$ such that either $1$ occurs exactly once in $\beta$ and $\lambda$ is $\beta$ with two more parts equal to $1$, or $2$ is not a part of $\beta$ and $\lambda$ is $\beta$ with one more part equal to $2$.

results.summary: Let $f(n)$ be the number of ordered factorizations of $n$ into factors greater than $1$. Let $r \ge 1$ and $N \ge 2(r+1)$, that is, $1 \le r \le \lfloor (N-2)/2 \rfloor$, and put $M = 2(r+1)$. results.title: Adding equal parts to a Type-A double-perfect partition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $r \ge 1$ and $n \ge 2(r+1)$ be integers, and let $\lambda$ be a Type-A double-perfect partition of $n$ of order $r$. Then for every natural number $m$, the partition obtained from $\lambda$ by adding $m$ parts equal to $n - r$ is a Type-A double-perfect partition of $n + m(n - r)$ of order $r$.

results.title: Inserting copies of a part into a double-perfect partition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $r \ge 1$, $n \ge 2(r+1)$, and let $\lambda$ be a double-perfect partition of $n$ of order $r$. For every $m \ge 0$, adding $m$ parts equal to $n - r$ to $\lambda$ gives a double-perfect partition of $n + m(n - r)$ of order $r$.

results.title: Adding a copy of the largest part to a double-perfect partition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $r \ge 1$, $n \ge 2(r+1)$, and let $\lambda$ be a double-perfect partition of $n$ of order $r$ whose largest part $\ell$ is not $r + 1$. Then $\lambda$ with one more part $\ell$ is a double-perfect partition of $n + \ell$ of order $r$. results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f(m)$ be the number of ordered factorizations of $m$ into factors greater than $1$. Then $u_r(N)$ equals $f(N-r) + (f(M) - 2f(r+1)) f((N-r)/(r+1)) - (f(M) - f(r+1)) f((N-r)/M)$ if $N \equiv r \pmod M$,…

results.title: Filipponi's binomial-sum formula, without range conditions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $r$ and $s$ let $f_r(s) = \sum_{j=0}^{s} \binom{r-j}{j}$, where $\binom{r-j}{j}$ is read as $0$ when $j > r$. Then for all natural numbers $n$, $h$ and $k$, $f_{n+2h}(k+h) = \sum_{j=0}^{h} \binom{h}{j} f_{n+j}(k+j)$.

results.title: Filipponi's binomial-sum formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $r$ and $s$ let $f_r(s) = \sum_{j=0}^{s} \binom{r-j}{j}$, where $\binom{r-j}{j}$ is read as $0$ when $j > r$. If $n$, $h$ and $k$ are natural numbers with $h \le n$ and $2k \le n - h$, then $f_{n+2h}(k+h) = \sum_{j=0}^{h} \binom{h}{j} f_{n+j}(k+j)$.

results.title: Girth-five extremal number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, $\mathrm{ex}(n; \{C_3, C_4\})$ is the largest number of edges of a simple graph on $n$ vertices whose girth is at least $5$, that is, which contains no triangle and no four-cycle (OEIS A006856). An acyclic graph has infinite girth, so the empty graph always qualifies.

results.title: Girth-five extremal numbers up to twenty vertices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $n = 1, 2, \dots, 20$ the girth-five extremal numbers $\mathrm{ex}(n; \{C_3, C_4\})$, the largest numbers of edges of a simple graph on $n$ vertices that contains no triangle and no four-cycle, are, in order, $0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 16, 18, 21, 23, 26, 28, 31, 34, 38, 41$.

results.title: Girth-five extremal number on fifty vertices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The girth-five extremal number $\mathrm{ex}(50; \{C_3, C_4\})$, the largest number of edges of a simple graph on $50$ vertices that contains no triangle and no four-cycle, equals $175$.

results.title: Tournaments
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$. A relation $T$ on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is a tournament when $T(x, x)$ holds for no $x$ and, for all distinct $x$ and $y$, exactly one of $T(x, y)$ and $T(y, x)$ holds.

results.title: Transitivity on a vertex set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $T$ be a relation on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $S$ be a set of its elements. Then $T$ is transitive on $S$ when, for all $x, y, z \in S$, $T(x, y)$ and $T(y, z)$ imply $T(x, z)$. For a tournament $T$ this says that the subtournament of $T$ on $S$ is transitive.

results.title: Transitive subtournament number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $f(n)$ is the largest $m$ such that every tournament $T$ on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is transitive on some set of exactly $m$ vertices, that is, contains a transitive subtournament on $m$ vertices.

results.title: Erdős Problem 1216 (the Erdős–Moser formula)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every $n \ge 1$, $f(n) = \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1$, where $f(n)$ is the largest $m$ such that every tournament on $n$ vertices contains a transitive subtournament on $m$ vertices.

results.title: Erdős Problem 1216 is false
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: It is not the case that $f(n) = \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1$ for every $n \ge 1$, where $f(n)$ is the largest $m$ such that every tournament on $n$ vertices contains a transitive subtournament on $m$ vertices.

results.title: The backward arcs of $T^*$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The backward arcs of $T^*$. The list of ordered pairs $(5, 0)$, $(5, 2)$, $(4, 1)$, $(3, 0)$ of vertices in $\{0, \dots, 5\}$. These are the arcs of the six-vertex tournament $T^*$ that go from a larger to a smaller vertex: $6 \to 1$, $6 \to 3$, $5 \to 2$ and $4 \to 1$ in the source's labelling $1, \dots, 6$, with every vertex lowered by one.

results.title: The six-vertex tournament $T^*$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The six-vertex tournament $T^*$. The tournament $T^*$ is the relation on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, 5\}$ with an arc $i \to j$ if and only if either $(i, j)$ is one of the backward arcs $(5, 0)$, $(5, 2)$, $(4, 1)$, $(3, 0)$, or $i < j$ and $(j, i)$ is not a backward arc.

results.title: Containing $T^*$ as a subtournament
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Containing $T^*$ as a subtournament. A relation $T$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ contains $T^*$ when there is an injective map $f$ from the vertex set $\{0, \dots, 5\}$ of $T^*$ to $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that for all vertices $i, j$ of $T^*$, $i \to j$ in $T^*$ if and only if $T(f(i), f(j))$ holds.

results.title: The Erdős–Hajnal problem for the tournament $T^*$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Erdős–Hajnal problem for the tournament $T^*$. There is a real number $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every natural number $n$ and every tournament $T$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that does not contain $T^*$ as a subtournament, there is a set $S$ of vertices on which $T$ is transitive with $|S| \ge n^{\varepsilon}$.

results.title: Efficient Domination instances
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of EFFICIENT DOMINATION is a pair $(n, E)$ of a natural number $n$, the number of vertices, and a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers, the edges.

results.title: Graph of an Efficient Domination instance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an instance $(n, E)$, its graph is the simple graph on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ in which distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent when $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ belongs to $E$.

results.title: Well-formed Efficient Domination instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, E)$ is well formed when the list $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(a, b)$ in $E$ satisfies $a < n$, $b < n$ and $a \ne b$, and $(b, a)$ does not belong to $E$.

results.title: Instances with an efficient dominating set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, E)$ of EFFICIENT DOMINATION is feasible when its graph has an efficient dominating set (a perfect code): a set $S$ of vertices such that every vertex $v$ has exactly one vertex $u \in S$ with $u = v$ or $u$ adjacent to $v$.

results.title: EFFICIENT DOMINATION (PERFECT CODE) as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decision problem EFFICIENT DOMINATION accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of instances, to an instance $(n, E)$ that is well formed and whose graph has an efficient dominating set. Bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.

results.title: EFFICIENT DOMINATION (PERFECT CODE) is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decision problem EFFICIENT DOMINATION belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
